title: My AI Agent Isn't Allowed to Decide Anything
why_read: A first-person account of building a constrained decision-support agent for media production scheduling, with some real rule-based-versus-AI design discussion.
analysis: The author describes a hackathon project, Shot-Delivery Guardian, that helps reorder work in a video/film post-production pipeline when deadlines are at risk, but deliberately keeps final decisions rule-based rather than letting an AI model choose freely. The stated design principle, that the AI only surfaces options while a hard-coded rule layer enforces business constraints so it can never violate a client agreement or deadline dependency, is a genuinely useful pattern for building trustworthy AI-assisted tools. The reported metrics (3 out of 5 correct picks, zero broken rules) are informal and hackathon-scale rather than rigorously benchmarked. It's a reasonable case study on agent guardrails but not deeply technical or broadly generalizable as written.
